name: Bánh bèo Cù Lao Chàm
summary: Bánh bèo Cù Lao Chàm is a small steamed rice cake in a cup, with a soft shrimp-and-pork topping, eaten with a bamboo knife. Báo Quảng Nam, carried by the Hội An World Heritage centre, describes the cake. The centre’s 16 September 2025 study names it as afternoon food and prints no method of its own. No date and no price were printed on the cake note.
origin: Cham Islands. Steamed rice cakes on Tân Hiệp, ground with Cham well water.
texture: Báo Quảng Nam says ordinary rice, soaked and ground with Cham well water, steams in cups over a charcoal fire until a swirl shows in the middle. The topping of shrimp, pork, and wood-ear mushroom stays soft, not dry. A brown sweet cake is served in some stalls and is still eaten with the salty topping.
taste: The same note says the topping tastes of salty fish sauce made from island fish, and of sweet shrimp.
howToEat: A tray is 6 to 10 cups. The seller gives a small bamboo knife, not chopsticks and not a spoon. Cut the cake and spear a piece.
The 16 September 2025 study places it in the afternoon, with bánh xèo chả cá, bánh canh, and mì Quảng. A stall hour is Check on arrival. A current price is Check on arrival.
where: The Bai Lang coast road and the stalls by Giếng Xóm Cấm in Bai Ong, where the 16 September 2025 study places the afternoon food. Báo Quảng Nam names no shop.

seoDescription: Small steamed rice cakes with a soft shrimp topping, cut with a bamboo knife. Afternoon food on the Bai Lang coast road. A stall price is Check on arrival.
